# S64 — slicer log has no per-item filter

**Findings:** dogfooding: after note/done I wanted one item's history, but log takes only --limit and shows everything. Add slicer log --item ID (repeatable) to scope history; pairs with find and note. · **Size:**  · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

`slicer log` takes only `--limit` and prints the whole history, so answering "what happened to
this one item?" (after note/done/set) means scanning everything. Friction filed dogfooding.

## Files

- src/slicer/cli.py: `cmd_log` gains a `--item` filter; registration adds the flag.
- tests/test_cli.py; README.md, docs/agents.md.

## Failing tests

## Implement

Add a repeatable `--item ID` to `log` that scopes history to those items, applied before the
existing timestamp sort and `--limit`. Permissive: an unknown or purged id yields no rows
rather than an error. Empty result reports "no history for <ids>".

## Check

`slicer log --item S02` shows only S02; repeated `--item` includes each; `--item` composes with
`--limit`; an id with no history exits 0. Focused log tests, the unit suite, slicer check, and
git diff --check.
